body:
Lee Kyu-hong has taken over at the NPS after previously leading Korea Teachers’ Pension (Image: NPS)

South Korea’s National Pension Service has brought on board Lee Kyu-hong as its new chief investment officer for a two-year term beginning 15 September, according to a statement from the pension fund.

Having spent most of his three-decade career at private asset managers with international partners, Lee joins NPS from a senior advisory role at law firm Shin & Kim, following four years as chief investment officer of Korea Teachers’ Pension.

NPS’s reserves grew to 1,866 trillion won ($1.4 trillion) by the end of June, up from 1,458 trillion won at the end of 2025, after a 27.22 percent investment return in the first half of this year — the fund’s strongest-ever six-month performance, according to Korea Herald.

The fund has become one of Asia’s most active cross-border and domestic real estate investors, with recent activity spanning Australian retail, Korean office and logistics assets, and a global platform-investing venture with a US manager.

Career In Asset Management

Lee most recently served as a senior advisor in the corporate finance division of law firm Shin & Kim, a role he held from 2024 until his appointment at the NPS.

Korea’s NPS is among the world’s largest pension investors (Image: NPS)

Prior to that, he spent four years as chief investment officer of Korea’s Teachers’ Pension, where the fund posted investment returns of 11.15 percent, 11.49 percent and 11.95 percent in its first three years under his leadership, according to the Korea Herald.

Before moving into public pension management, Lee served as chief investment officer of NH-Amundi Asset Management, a joint venture between South Korea’s NongHyup Financial Group and France’s Amundi, from 2013 to 2018, after an earlier stint at Eastspring Asset Management, then the Asia-focused arm of the UK’s Prudential Group and now known as Cadian Asset Management.

Born in 1966, Lee holds a business administration degree from Yonsei University and an MBA in finance from New York University’s Stern School of Business.

The NPS opened its recruitment process for the CIO post in June, according to an announcement at the time, with Lee’s predecessor, Seo Won-joo, having stayed on to facilitate the transition.

Seo, who had served as chief investment officer at the NPS since December 2022, had his original two-year term extended through December 2025, before staying on this year. Seo is credited with having led NPS through a recovery from a record annual loss in 2022.

Global Property Footprint

With Korean investors playing a growing role in Asia Pacific markets, a joint venture between NPS and a Lendlease-managed vehicle in January sold Australia’s Erina Fair shopping centre for $604 million, a record for the sole-ownership sale of an Australian retail facility.

In its home market the NPS that same month agreed to buy Incheon’s Arenas Yeongjong Logistics Center from Singapore’s Straits Trading and Seoul-based IGIS Asset Management for KRW 432 billion ($300 million).

In February 2025, the NPS made its largest-ever single domestic real estate investment, paying KRW 2.3 trillion ($1.6 billion) for the One Grove office complex in western Seoul. The previous month, the fund committed $800 million to a real estate platform-investment venture with Neuberger Berman’s Almanac Realty Investors, aimed at building stakes in real estate operating platforms globally.

NPS’s October 2024 investment alongside Koramco, GS Engineering & Construction and City Core in the redevelopment of The Exchange Seoul in central Seoul has drawn separate scrutiny this year. South Korea’s health and welfare ministry asked NPS in July to investigate a leak of confidential Alternative Investment Committee deliberations concerning the deal. The NPS has since set up a dedicated task force to examine the matter, according to Seoul Economic Daily and KED Global.
